purpose: Compare current OldScanner and installed MDVx PMR buffering/retention and recommend the explicit Bella PMR memory lifetime.
userRequest: Are PMR files stored in memory, read once, etc - the same way? How does MediaMuster do it? how does mdvx do it? how SHOULD we do it?
status: PMR read-once/extract/release memory workflow approved by the user on 2026-10-21. Research remains bounded static evidence, not runtime implementation or a measured performance result.

approval.userStatement: OK, let's lock that in for Bella: read each PMR once into memory, extract only what we need, and release the buffer. What's next?
approval.decision: Adopt recommendedBellaWorkflow below as the explicit PMR single-capture and temporary-memory lifetime, preserving approved PMR set selection/fallback, encodings, full identities and four-job maximum.
approval.scope: Requirements approval. Separate four-MDB maximum and approved MDB memory workflow remain unchanged. The narrower MDB-version baseline is still proposed. OldScanner stays active and implementation follows the remaining requirements review.

historicalPolicyStatusNote: Embedded source/native receipts remain research snapshots, including their recommendation wording. The top-level approval supersedes pending status for recommendedBellaWorkflow only; research limits and future verification remain unchanged.

mediaMuster.audit: Current active OldScanner PMR disk and RAM lifecycle
mediaMuster.method: Read-only source audit, no builds, app execution or media writes.

findings.claim: Active app delegates to ScanEngine and ScanCoordinator; database candidates handled sequentially in normal loop, not four concurrent.

For each scheduled PMR, QFile opens once and DatabaseImage captures complete file bytes from start in bounded <=1MiB reads. One content capture pass per candidate, not a single read syscall. Final extent check. No PMR reread loop in normal scan.
QBuffer shares image QByteArray without duplicating full bytes, parser reads from RAM device.

Parser walks legacy then extension in physical order; both sets produce raw per-field properties/objects/relationships. Per-field encoding bytes copied from RAM buffer and decoded fields retained. This is one grammar invocation plus a projection pass, not duplicate full PMR parse or more disk reads.

SourceReceipt keeps only outcome/readreason/snapshot/container/diagnostics. Full RAM image and ParsedSource objects released when prepareDatabase returns. Qt shared bytearrays mean aliases are not necessarily duplicate allocations.

Projected per-field rawValue encoding survives into match evidence, with source/property/object/read/encoding explanations. Both old/new sets have separate projected entries. PMR-name lookup built per source after preparation. These projections/indexes live until coordinator returns.

ScanResult evidence incl selected PMR per-field rawValue exists through final matching and OldScanner row formatting. doScan returns compact UI rows/reconciliationissues/cancelled/time only; no ScanResult owner, wholePMR or MediaEvidence is stored in final UI rows.

limits: No performance or allocation measurements performed; source ownership proves lifecycle, not measured peak RSS.

Normal single scan and unique discovered candidates inspected. OS caching and physical disk transport not observable from this audit. A new user scan rereads its databases; no persistent PMR byte cache found on this path.
Postread source QFileInfo checks are metadata checks, not PMR byte rereads.
Same backing QByteArray can be implicitly shared, so do not claim every rawValue alias allocates another byte copy.

mdvx.purpose: Read-only installed MDVx PMR acquisition, parsing, retention and cleanup audit for Bella requirements.

method.native: Fresh bounded disassembly with xcrun llvm-objdump --macho --arch=arm64 --disassemble --dis-symname; native symbols from nm. No executable or private parser invocation.

facts.finding: One whole PMR content acquisition per PMRFile dataWithContentsOfURL invocation; retained NSData input with borrowed byte pointer.
instructions: 0x10003a460..3a478: operation allocates PMRFile and invokes dataWithContentsOfURL once
facts.limits: One logical Foundation whole-file read, not proof of exactly one kernel read or physical disk access. NSData storage implementation is Foundation owned.

facts.finding: FillItem advances a position cursor through base records and, if the equal-count version16 resynchronization succeeds, through appended records from the same input buffer. This is not a second file read.
instructions: 0x100039e88..39ed0: after base item count inspect appended version/count
0x100039f88..39f98: change parser state to16 and reset current item, advance past extension header
0x10003a154..3a168: pass record bytes/length/version to item initializer
facts.limits: Both sets materialize item objects in this path; Bella approved whole-set preference is different.

facts.finding: Every PMR item copies record bytes into an independently owned mutable data object before field extraction. Names/project become separate NSString fields. Modern IDs are additionally copied into fixed32-byte fields.
instructions: 0x1000304cc..304dc: bytes and mutableBytes from copied data
facts.limits: The stored mutable bytes may be byte-swapped in place; this is a retained copy, not necessarily bit-for-bit untouched input.

facts.finding: The operation retains its PMRFile throughout directory work then relinquishes it at cleanup; PMRFile destructor releases the whole NSData and saved currentpath. Items do not depend on that whole buffer.
facts.limits: ARC/Foundation ownership release is established; no runtime RSS measurement or precise allocator page-return timing was tested.

facts.finding: Copied record buffers and item decoded strings remain owned by each output item until that item is released; item destructor clears strong reference to+0x70.
instructions: 0x100031678..31698: clear project+0x80, filename+0x78 and copied record+0x70

facts.finding: Folder operation gathers output items, appends batch under core lock, then releases its local output array.
Ordinary all-scan path deduplicates after operation queue completion.
instructions: 0x10004ba7c..4baa4: replace output array with nonequal tree data array
facts.limits: Does not establish exact duplicate winner here. Existing identity review documents comparator binding separately.

facts.finding: Configured queue maximum6 is used by ordinary PMR jobs.
facts.limits: Six concurrent operations permitted, not guaranteed six active OS threads/CPUs; MDB work may be inside same operation when enabled.

recommendationForBella.status: Recommendation; preserve existing approved four-job limit and whole-set/text/identity rules.
workflow: Acquire a PMR once into one scoped owned QByteArray using checked QFile reads.
Traverse bounded framing in memory; locate appended v16 through old variable-length records without creating two complete decoded result sets.
Decode/materialize only the usable chosen whole set: prefer v16, fallback to complete older set if missing/unusable.
Keep owned selected filename/project values and full normalized IDs; no borrowed view may escape input lifetime.
Do not retain a separate raw record-byte copy per result or unused DTM.
Drop PMR input buffer and framing temporaries immediately after independent PMR results are produced, without keeping them until MDB/header/table work finishes.
Max4 simultaneous PMR acquisitions/parses; independent MDB cap4 as separately approved.
recommendationForBella.qualification: A logical read-once acquisition can require multiple read calls/partial reads. In-memory framing and validation may require more than one cursor pass. No performance guarantee or benchmark result.

recommendedBellaWorkflow.status: Explicit PMR single-capture lifetime approved on 2026-10-21. Existing PMR set/field/validation/identity rules and four-job maximum remain approved; MDB memory workflow/four-job maximum remain approved.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.capture: One complete immutable job-owned PMR capture per ordinary unchanged source; close source after capture. One capture is not necessarily one operating-system read call.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.locate: Follow known older-set framing safely in memory to find v16. No older-string decoding/materialization solely to locate the extension and no raw-byte hunting.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.selectedSet: Stage compact v16 results privately and publish only after the entire set passes. If absent/unusable, discard rejected staging and try older set from the same capture. Do not mix sets or keep both decoded result sets.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.retained: Owned Filename/Project strings under approved encodings; complete binary file/master identities via approved normalization; necessary compact status. Ignore DTM beyond checked skipping.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.lifetime: Release PMR image, bounded views and parsing temporaries when selected compact results own required data. No per-item raw PMR copies; no borrowed pointers/views/hash keys may escape.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.languageAndTools: Fresh C++17/Qt6.5.3 small value types, scoped ownership/RAII, checked bounds/counts and task-local state. No C++20/23 features required.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.concurrency: Keep existing approved maxima fourPMR/fourMDB. Separate source-type maxima can overlap, so combined peak memory/storage contention need measurement. No whole-scan fixed RAM guarantee.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.physicalInventory: PMR usability does not determine whether physical media are listed. Existing MDB read and media-header rules remain unchanged.
recommendedBellaWorkflow.performance: Reduce avoidable per-field materialization/copies and double-set interpretation; neither compared ordinary path repeatedly opens PMR per physical row. No measured performance advantage claimed.

limits: Native/source lifetimes establish ownership behavior, not allocator RSS or measured scan performance.
Fresh size observations are stat-only for six known paths; no new PMR content hashes or parsing in this subtask.
Current bytearray aliases can share backing storage; do not assume every assignment is another allocation.
MDVx one Foundation acquisition is not proof of one kernel read or disk access.
No app/private API, parser test suite, malformed-input execution or live media write performed.
